newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds firmer in late quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds firmer in late quiet trading.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities clung to slight gains late in the session in tandem with U.S. Treasuries, according to traders.
"We're pretty much in line (with Treasuries), but I guess you'd say on a spread basis we're a little bit tighter," said a pass-through trader.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7-1/2 percent paper was 4/32 firmer at 99-20/32 to yield 97 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were 5/32 higher at 99-21/32, while Freddie Mac paper was up 3/32 at 99-25/32.
Ten-year Treasuries were 4/32 higher at 99-26/32 to yield 6.65 percent.
Traders said the mortgage-backed market was fairly quiet on Monday.

No key U.S. economic data were released on Monday, but on Tuesday, U.S. retail sales is due out at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. Economists polled by Reuters, on average, expected sales fell 0.3 percent in April after rising 0.1 percent in March.
There are "a lot of numbers this week and then people are waiting to see what the (Federal Reserve) is going to do next week," the pass-through trader said.
Fed policymakers will next meet on May 20. On March 25, they had voted to hike the federal funds rate by 25 basis point to 5.50 percent.
Despite the quiet tenor of mortgage-backed trading on Monday, a trader at a midwest bank cited continuing demand for pass-throughs with coupons of 8.5 percent and higher.
"There's still a fair amount of interest in this premium paper," the trader said. "People don't believe this rally is going to be here to stay."
